dh.headline: Kadhi chronicles: A culinary journey through regional variations and history
dh.subheadline: From Gujarat's fajeto to Bihar's phulauri and Andhra's majjiga pulusu, the yogurt-based curry finds a place on most Indian plates.
dh.imageCaption: A popular way to relish kadhi is to add pakoda to it.

dh.headline: A taste of winter: Gajjak, Sandesh, Malaiyo & more
dh.subheadline: Swatee Jog pens five traditional Indian winter delicacies that bring together seasonal ingredients, comforting flavours, and age-old culinary traditions

dh.headline: Karunadotsava | Darshinis, military hotels, bakeries: A food lover's guide to Bengaluru's iconic eateries and flavours
dh.subheadline: These iconic eateries offer a taste of the city’s enduring food traditions and also have a history that one can learn and be proud of.

dh.headline: Partition, food & Memory: Echoes from an undivided kitchen
dh.subheadline: When refugees arrived in Calcutta, food was not the first thing on their minds. Many had fled with whatever little they could carry, leaving behind familiar ways of life.

dh.headline: Let the good times fizz! Four easy-to-make mocktails to liven up your festive parties
dh.subheadline: Swatee Jog shares four easy-to-make mocktail recipes featuring jamun, mango, blueberry and green apple to keep your celebrations bubbling with flavour.

dh.headline: Steamed to perfection: The secret behind Palakkad's famous Ramassery idli
dh.subheadline: The selection of rice is very important in making Ramassery idlis. The taste depends on the boiling of paddy.

dh.headline: The obbattu: Tracing the layered history of Karnataka’s festive sweet
dh.subheadline: From medieval culinary texts to regional variations made with lentils, coconut, peanuts and sweet potato, obbattu has evolved over centuries, reflecting Karnataka’s diverse food traditions.
dh.imageCaption: The holige or obbattu is Karnataka's sought-after sweet.

dh.headline: Odisha on a platter: Exploring the traditions, flavours and culinary heritage of Odia cuisine
dh.subheadline: Odia cuisine is not shaped by a single tradition — its many flavours have been defined from the region's forests, sea and rivers, apart from temples and royal kitchens.
dh.imageCaption: A typical Odia thaali, with the pakhala bhat, cooked rice lightly fermented in waer.

dh.headline: Breaking bread: A taste of tradition in Georgia
dh.subheadline: The classic Imeruli khachapuri, originating in Imereti, is round and filled with cheese. Megruli khachapuri from Samegrelo has cheese stuffed inside as well as melted over the top.

dh.headline: Floral cocktails: Bars give traditional flowers a modern twist
dh.subheadline: Beyond the decorative rim, flowers have become the new flavour baseline in contemporary mixology.
dh.imageCaption: The drink, Mehrauli, which on Sidecar's signature Dear Delhi menu.

dh.headline: Vegetarian, but make it fancy: Bengaluru's new-age dining scene
dh.subheadline: More spaces in South Bengaluru now serve experimental food beyond paneer and mushroom.
dh.imageCaption: At Eatinn Love Trattoria in Jayanagar the focus is on vegetarian Italian food.

dh.headline: A spoonful, but with context: Why urban India is hungry for food history and science
dh.subheadline: A guava that tastes off, rice that smells of its soil, a pickle that makes one wonder about caste history: curiosity about food is taking urban Indian diners far beyond the plate. They are reading, tasting, questioning and discovering that every bite has its own backstory.
dh.imageCaption: Urban Indians are looking at their plates with renewed curiosity.

dh.headline: A kadubu by any other name…
dh.subheadline: From jackfruit stuffing to modern-day fillings made of dates, chocolate and rose flavours, the dish has lent itself to creativity rather well.
dh.imageCaption: Modakas are an invariable part of a festive meal during Ganesha Chaturthi.

dh.headline: Before Biryani, there was Khichadi: The ancient story of India’s one-pot meals
dh.subheadline: From simple rice and lentil dishes to pulao, tehari and the layered biryani, one-pot meals are nutrition-rich, convenient and flavourful. Zubin D'Souza writes about the layered history of one pot meals, some of which appear in ancient texts
dh.imageCaption: Tehari, a one-pot meal made of rice and vegetables, is considered a frugal meal.

pv.headline: ಸಬ್ಬಸಿಗೆ ಸವಿರುಚಿ: ಬಗೆ ಬಗೆ ಸಬ್ಬಸಿಗೆ ರೆಸಿಪಿಗಳು
ಕ್ಲೌಡ್ ಕಿಚನ್‌ನಿಂದ ಬದುಕು ಕಂಡುಕೊಂಡ ಬೆಂಗಳೂರಿನ ರಾಕೇಶ್, ಯಾಮಿನಿ ದಂಪತಿ

authors.name: ವೇಣುಗೋಪಾಲ ಕೆ.
authors.bio: 18 ವರ್ಷಗಳ ಪತ್ರಿಕೋದ್ಯಮದ ಅನುಭವ. ಸುದ್ದಿ ಮನೆಯ ಯಾವುದೇ ವಿಭಾಗಗಳಲ್ಲೂ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡಬಲ್ಲ ನೈಪುಣ್ಯ. ಷೇರುಪೇಟೆ, ಸಿನಿಮಾ, ರಾಜಕೀಯ, ಕ್ರಿಕೆಟ್ ಆಸಕ್ತಿ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರಗಳು. ಸುವರ್ಣ ನ್ಯೂಸ್, ನ್ಯೂಸ್ 18 ಕನ್ನಡ, ಟೈಮ್ಸ್ ಆಫ್ ಇಂಡಿಯಾ, ವೆಬ್ ದುನಿಯಾ ಸೇರಿದಂತೆ ಸುದ್ದಿ ವಾಹಿನಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸುದ್ದಿ ಜಾಲತಾಣಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡಿದ್ದಾರೆ.  ಸದ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ಪ್ರಜಾವಾಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹಿರಿಯ ಉಪಸಂಪಾದಕ.

tags.name: Karunadotsava Story
tags.meta-description: ಕನ್ನಡ ರಾಜ್ಯೋತ್ಸವದ ವಿಶೇಷ ಸಂಭ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕದ ಇತಿಹಾಸ, ಕನ್ನಡ ಭಾಷೆಯ ಶ್ರೀಮಂತಿಕೆ, ನಾಡಿನ ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತಿ, ಪರಂಪರೆ ಹಾಗೂ ಕನ್ನಡಿಗರ ಹೆಮ್ಮೆಯ ಸಾಧನೆಗಳ ಕುರಿತ ವಿಶೇಷ ಲೇಖನಗಳನ್ನು ಪ್ರಜಾವಾಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಓದಿ.
tags.meta-title: Kannada Rajyotsava Stories: ಕರುನಾಡೋತ್ಸವದ ವಿಶೇಷ ಕಥನಗಳು | Prajavani
